content: Living Water International is a non-profit organization dedicated to assisting underserved communities in implementing projects related to water, sanitation, and hygiene education. Since its establishment in 1991, Living Water International has successfully completed over 4,200 water projects, which now provide clean water to approximately 6 million people on a daily basis. The organization operates in 25 countries, including Mexico, Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama, Haiti, Peru, Brazil, Liberia, Sierra Leone, Ghana, Nigeria, Central African Republic, Angola, Namibia, Zambia, Sudan, Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Rwanda, India, and Romania. The mission of Living Water International is to demonstrate the love of God by helping communities gain access to desperately needed clean water while also sharing the living water of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, which they believe satisfies the deepest human thirst. Living Water International is a partner of the ONE Campaign, which focuses on addressing global poverty and preventable diseases. Globally, unsafe water and inadequate sanitation contribute to 8 million deaths annually, with 90% of these deaths occurring among children. The World Health Organization (WHO) has emphasized that improving access to safe water, along with better health and hygiene practices, could significantly reduce the burden of disease in developing countries. Similarly, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has identified unsafe water and poor sanitation as major drivers of global poverty and inequality. These issues not only claim millions of lives but also destroy livelihoods, compromise human dignity, and hinder economic growth. The human costs are disproportionately borne by poor populations, particularly women and children. In many parts of the world, the most effective and reliable solution for providing safe water is drilling wells and installing contained water delivery systems, often equipped with hand pumps. However, remote areas are frequently inaccessible to large, truck-mounted drilling rigs. To address this challenge, Harry Westmoreland, a co-founder of Living Water International, developed the LS-100 drill rig in 1989. This portable, cost-effective rig is designed for soft formations and can be easily dismantled and transported via pickup truck or boat. It can also be operated by a single individual. An upgraded version, the LS-200, is also available. In some regions, water is abundant but contaminated. In such cases, Living Water International employs BioSand Water Filter technology, developed by Dr. David Manz of Calgary, Alberta, Canada. This technology utilizes a slow sand filtration process. Contaminated water is poured into the top of the filter, where it passes through layers of sand and gravel by gravity before being collected at the bottom through a standpipe. A biological layer forms in the top one to two centimeters of sand, which aids in filtration by digesting organic contaminants, parasites, bacteria, and viruses. BioSand Water Filters are an effective and affordable solution for removing waterborne pathogens (such as helminths, parasites, bacteria, and viruses), particulate matter, color, dissolved organic carbon (DOC), biochemical oxygen demand (BOD), organic toxins, and inorganic toxins like arsenic and mercury. Kofi Annan, former United Nations Secretary-General, once stated, We shall not finally defeat AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria, or any of the other infectious diseases that plague the developing world until we have also won the battle for safe drinking water, sanitation, and basic health care. Additionally, the United Nations General Comment No. 15 (2002) on the Right to Water declares, The human right to water entitles everyone to sufficient, safe, acceptable, physically accessible, and affordable water for personal and domestic uses.
